title: Mosaic: Detection and Categorization of I/O Patterns in HPC Applications
problem: HPC applications exhibit diverse and complex I/O behavior patterns that are difficult to understand and characterize, hindering effective optimization of I/O performance as the gap between computing power and storage I/O performance widens.
motivation: Understanding application I/O behavior is essential for optimizing storage resource utilization and bridging the compute-I/O performance gap in modern HPC systems.
method: Mosaic introduces an abstraction that characterizes I/O operations along three dimensions: periodicity (how often patterns repeat), temporality (timing of accesses), and metadata access patterns. Segmentation-based techniques are applied to automatically detect meaningful patterns from I/O traces, enabling rapid categorization of applications without manual analysis.
key_novelty: A systematic framework for automatically detecting and categorizing HPC application I/O behavior by abstracting operations into periodicity, temporality, and metadata access dimensions.
contributions: Abstraction framework for characterizing I/O operations in HPC applications
Segmentation-based techniques for automatic I/O pattern detection
Automated application categorization achieving 92% accuracy on real-world supercomputer traces
Validated approach using Blue Waters supercomputer I/O traces
primary_theme: Automatic I/O pattern detection and application categorization in HPC
